title: Cinematography and Video Synthesis
answer: Text to video, virtual lensing, digital doubles, storyboarding and frame interpolation.

children.name: Text to Video, Physics and Continuity
children.blurb: Text to video with physics and continuity concerns generating moving images from natural language prompts where objects obey plausible physical rules and remain consistent across frames.

children.name: Virtual Camera and Lensing
children.blurb: Virtual camera and lensing covers the simulation of optical and mechanical camera properties inside synthetic and AI-generated video.

children.name: Face Replacement and Digital Doubles
children.blurb: Face replacement and digital doubles cover techniques for swapping one person's face onto another performer's body, creating a synthetic likeness of an actor for stunts, de-aging, or posthumous appearances, and generating fully synthetic human faces for background or principal roles.

children.name: Storyboarding and Pre-visualization
children.blurb: AI storyboarding and pre-visualization covers the use of generative image and video models to turn scripts, shot lists, and director's notes into rough visual sequences before production.

children.name: Frame Interpolation and Restoration
children.blurb: Frame interpolation creates intermediate frames between existing frames to increase temporal resolution or smooth motion.

sections.body: This field covers tools that turn written descriptions into moving images, simulate camera movement and lenses, replace faces with digital doubles, plan shots before filming, and create missing frames between existing ones. Current work is practical rather than theoretical: video models generate short clips from prompts, virtual camera systems let a director move a viewpoint after a scene is captured, and face replacement is used in post-production to match stunt performers or de-age actors. Storyboarding tools turn script pages into rough animated sequences, while frame interpolation smooths slow motion or repairs damaged footage. The site tracks 1000 live video models, which gives a sense of how crowded this area has become.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Short text to video clips of a few seconds are now common, but longer scenes with consistent physics, object permanence, and character identity remain unsolved. Virtual camera and lensing can convincingly move through a static or lightly animated scene, yet complex reflections and occlusions still break. Face replacement and digital doubles work well under controlled lighting and frontal angles, but fail on extreme profiles, fast motion, or fine hair detail. Storyboarding and pre-visualization produce useful rough drafts, not finished shots, and often need a human artist to correct composition and intent. Frame interpolation and restoration are the most mature, but they still introduce artifacts in fast action or textured backgrounds. The honest limit is that none of these tools yet replace a cinematographer or editor for final, broadcast quality work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how prompts become moving images should start with Text to Video, Physics and Continuity, which explains the core generation and its current failure modes. Virtual Camera and Lensing covers the separate problem of controlling viewpoint, focal length, and depth of field after capture, and pairs naturally with the first page when planning a synthetic shot. Face Replacement and Digital Doubles is the page for actor substitution, de-aging, and consent or rights questions, and it connects to the virtual camera work because a digital double still needs a plausible camera. Storyboarding and Pre-visualization sits earlier in a production, turning a script into rough moving frames, and is useful for directors who want to test blocking before any final asset exists. Frame Interpolation and Restoration is the most technical and least creative page, focused on repairing or extending footage, and it often serves as a cleanup step after the other tools have produced their output.
